claims.text: Incorporating 1–3 at.% silicon into bulk TiB2 and then pre-oxidizing it will form an optimized, continuous SiO2 layer.
Applying a silicon-containing surface coating to TiB2 and then pre-oxidizing it will form an optimized, continuous SiO2 layer.
The silicon-modification and pre-oxidation intervention will significantly improve the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of TiB2-based components.
Controlled pre-oxidation will generate a continuous and adherent SiO2 layer at the component surface.
Controlled pre-oxidation will generate SiO2 along TiB2 grain boundaries.
During pre-oxidation, incorporated silicon oxidizes before the component is exposed to molten aluminum.
The resulting SiO2 is stable under the proposed molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
A continuous SiO2 layer acts as a passivating barrier against molten aluminum.
The SiO2 barrier impedes reactive penetration of molten aluminum into the TiB2-based component.
The SiO2 barrier minimizes dissolution or reaction of TiB2 in molten aluminum and thereby lowers its corrosion rate.
At approximately 700 °C, silicon-modified and pre-oxidized TiB2 may exhibit more than a 30% reduction in mass loss relative to the baseline.
Silicon-modified and pre-oxidized TiB2 will retain greater microstructural stability after molten-aluminum exposure than baseline TiB2.
The protective effect should remain effective under controlled hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions near 700 °C for specified immersion durations.
Higher exposure temperatures or prolonged immersion may diminish the effectiveness of the SiO2 barrier.
Departures from the required pre-oxidation protocol may diminish the effectiveness of the SiO2 barrier.
Pre-oxidation may adversely affect the mechanical or thermal properties of the TiB2-based component.
